lines.en: label christmalloween2:
scene tsukiokamalloween3

: {size=-3}You see, Chinami, the key benefit of unlimited PTO is that it provides the {i}illusion{/i} of employee-centric viewpoints without actually sacrificing anything and ultimately having the {i}reverse{/i} effect on your minions. I mean staff.{/size}
lines.zh: {size=-3}你看，Chinami，无限带薪假的关键好处在于，它{i}营造{/i}出一种以员工为中心的错觉，实际上却什么都没牺牲，最终对你的仆从……我是说员工……产生{i}完全相反{/i}的效果。{/size}

lines.en: : Once you bring a finite amount into play, people feel incentivized to make use of it and actually take {i}more{/i} vacation days than they would without any sort of maximum at all.
lines.zh: 一旦引入一个上限，人们就会觉得非用不可，反而比完全没有上限时休{i}更多{/i}天假。

lines.en: : Chinami thinks it would be good for employee acquisition as well. She will take it up with our shareholders during the Q4 earnings report.
lines.zh: Chinami 觉得这对招聘员工也有好处。她会在第四季度财报上跟股东们提这事。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween2
: It appears that our monthly meeting has adjourned then! Excellent work today as always.
lines.zh: 看来我们的月度会议到此休会了！今天也一如既往地出色。

lines.en: : Thanks, Tsukasa! Chinami can’t help but wonder how our friends and family will react when they find out we bought Microsoft, though.
lines.zh: 谢谢，Tsukasa！不过 Chinami 忍不住好奇，等我们买下微软的事传出去，亲朋好友会是什么反应。

lines.en: : We’ll keep it a secret for now so they keep treating us like kids. But one day, when they least expect it, boom! We’re actually even wealthier than {i}they{/i} are!
lines.zh: 我们先保密，好让他们继续把我们当小孩。不过等哪天他们最意想不到的时候，砰！我们其实比{i}他们{/i}还有钱！

lines.en: : Chinami’s family isn’t wealthy at all! But she still understands what Tsukasa means.
lines.zh: Chinami 家一点也不有钱！不过她还是明白 Tsukasa 的意思。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween3
: When are you going to stop referring to yourself in the third person? You know I won’t tell anybody if you talk normally.
lines.zh: 你什么时候才不用第三人称称呼自己？你知道的，你要是正常说话，我不会告诉任何人。

lines.en: : When is Tsukasa going to start referring to Tsukasa in the third person because it’s more fun?
lines.zh: 那 Tsukasa 什么时候开始用第三人称称呼 Tsukasa？因为这样更好玩。

lines.en: : Tsukasa doesn’t think so.
lines.zh: Tsukasa 不这么认为。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween4
: Oh. Actually, that was kind of fun.
lines.zh: 哦。说起来，那样还挺好玩的。

lines.en: : See? Chinami is worried Tsukasa’s mom might think Tsukasa has some sort of degenerative brain disease if she starts doing that now, though.
lines.zh: 瞧？不过 Chinami 担心，要是 Tsukasa 现在开始这样，Tsukasa 的妈妈可能会以为她得了什么退化性脑病。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween5
: But maybe that’s a {i}good{/i} idea?! She’ll feel way worse about making you marry some old guy if your brain is dying!
lines.zh: 不过这也许是{i}个好{/i}主意？！要是你的脑子正在坏掉，她逼你嫁给某个老头子的时候会更过意不去！

lines.en: : I thought we agreed to not talk about that today in the spirit of Christmalloween?
lines.zh: 我们不是说好了，本着圣诞万圣节的精神，今天不谈这个吗？

lines.en: : If Tsukasa is going to talk to Chinami about sex all the time now, Chinami thinks it’s only fair that Chinami gets to talk about things she wants too. Even if they violate notarized agreements.
lines.zh: 既然 Tsukasa 现在整天要和 Chinami 聊性，Chinami 觉得自己也有权利聊她想聊的东西才公平。哪怕违反了经过公证的协议。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween6
: Fine. Then I suppose it can not be helped. Especially since you have acquired information I am inclined and motivated to trade for.
lines.zh: 好吧。那我看是没办法了。尤其是你手上已经有了我很想、也很有动力去交换的情报。

lines.en: : For the millionth time, Chinami doesn’t want to talk about her watching her big sister and Papa turn into rabid sex animals.
lines.zh: 我都说第一百万遍了，Chinami 不想聊她看着姐姐和爸爸变成发情的性爱野兽那件事。

lines.en: : Then I will have to do this the old fashioned way. By installing hidden cameras throughout your property while you are away so I can watch them on my own.
lines.zh: 那我只好用老办法了。趁你不在，在你家各处装隐藏摄像头，好让我自己看。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween7
: What kind of “old fashioned way” is that?! Keep your cameras out of Chinami’s house! She doesn’t want you peeping on her! Her days being numbered makes them stressful enough as is!
lines.zh: 这算哪门子「老办法」？！把你的摄像头撤出 Chinami 家！她才不想被你偷看！她本来就时日无多，已经够有压力了！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween8
: Why don’t you just stop being sick? Is there really no cure?
lines.zh: 你干脆别生病了不行吗？真的没法治吗？

lines.en: : Chinami isn’t technically sick at all. Her body just makes her {i}get{/i} sick really easily. That’s why she showed up today wearing a dog helmet.
lines.zh: 严格来说 Chinami 根本没病。只是她的身体特别容易让她{i}生病{/i}。所以她今天才会戴着一顶狗头盔来。

lines.en: : And probably why the cleaning crew was working overtime. I’m just kind of confused about how we can help mom’s cancer-friend but not you. Your thing seems way less serious than that.
lines.zh: 大概也是保洁队要加班的原因。我只是有点搞不懂，为什么我们能帮妈妈那个得了癌症的朋友，却帮不了你。你这毛病看起来可比那个轻多了。

lines.en: : Chinami doesn’t really understand either. But at least she doesn’t have a degenerative brain disease like Tsukasa.
lines.zh: Chinami 也不太明白。不过至少她没有像 Tsukasa 那样得退化性脑病。

lines.en: : If you only had a day left to live, what do you think you’d do?
lines.zh: 如果你只剩一天可活，你觉得你会做什么？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween9
: So dark! Chinami doesn’t like that question!
lines.zh: 太阴暗了！Chinami 不喜欢这个问题！

lines.en: : Really? I figured you’d already have an answer for it if your days really {i}are{/i} numbered.
lines.zh: 真的吗？我还以为如果你的日子真{i}是{/i}屈指可数，你早就想好答案了呢。

lines.en: : Well I- {i}she{/i} doesn’t! Chinami! Me! Bad Tsukasa! Go to your room!
lines.zh: 那我——{i}她{/i}没有！Chinami！我！坏 Tsukasa！回你房间去！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween10
: Fine. But {i}you’re{/i} coming with me. For I have learned of a place called the “dark web” that is immune to all forms of parental control!
lines.zh: 好吧。但{i}你{/i}得跟我一起来。因为我听说有个叫「暗网」的地方，对所有形式的家长控制都免疫！

lines.en: : Aaaaaaaahhhhhhhhh!
lines.zh: 啊啊啊啊啊啊啊！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween11
: Chinami, darling — please don’t scream like that. You’ll work yourself up and I don’t want you going home all weak and exhausted, okay?
lines.zh: Chinami，亲爱的——别那样叫。你会把自己折腾坏的，我可不想你回家时虚弱又疲惫，好吗？

lines.en: : Okay, Mrs. Tsukioka! I’m so glad that I have Tsukasa here to help me feel better! Who {i}knows{/i} what would happen if she was suddenly gone? I’d probably just die!
lines.zh: 好的，Tsukioka 夫人！我真高兴有 Tsukasa 在这儿让我好受些！要是她突然不在了，{i}谁又知道{/i}会怎样？我说不定会死掉！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween12
: Right...I’m sure that is exactly what would happen.
lines.zh: 是吗……我相信事情一定会是这样。

lines.en: : Codependency seems to run in that family. So I’m not entirely sure if that statement is as inaccurate as you subtly seem to be implying, Mother.
lines.zh: 那家人似乎有互相依赖的传统。所以我不太确定这话是不是像你含蓄暗示的那样不准确，母亲。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween13
: Oh? Is that a hint of sourness I detect in your voice, Touka? Has Chika’s {i}attachment{/i} to your beloved teacher finally taken its toll on you?
lines.zh: 哦？我怎么从你声音里听出一点酸味，Touka？Chika 对你那位亲爱的老师的{i}依恋{/i}，终于让你受不了了吗？

lines.en: : He is not my beloved {i}anything.{/i} Nor is he even my teacher at this point in time. That role has been inherited by someone who actually {i}cares{/i} about my education.
lines.zh: 他不是我亲爱的{i}任何东西{/i}。而且现在他也不再是我的老师了。那个角色已经由一个真正{i}关心{/i}我学业的人接手了。

lines.en: : Arakawa-Sensei would care as well if you’d only let him teach you the area in which he excels instead of throwing temper tantrums over it.
lines.zh: 只要你肯让 Arakawa 老师教他擅长的那个领域，而不是为这个大发脾气，他也会关心你的。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween14
: If you’re insisting that my reluctance to let a grown man teach my younger sister about sex is a “tantrum,” then perhaps our viewpoints on the matter are simply incompatible.
lines.zh: 如果你非要把我不愿让一个成年男人教我妹妹关于性的事称作「发脾气」，那也许我们在这件事上的看法根本就合不来。

lines.en: : I’m inclined to believe that was merely me acting as a rational human being instead of whatever you’re slowly turning into, though.
lines.zh: 不过我倒倾向于认为，那只是我作为一个理性的人在行事，而不是像你正在慢慢变成的那种东西。

lines.en: : A caring mother, of course. I only want what’s best for my girls.
lines.zh: 当然是变成一个关心孩子的母亲。我只想给我的女儿们最好的。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween15
: Right. And I suppose it’s {i}best{/i} for Tsukasa to be pawned off on whatever brand of perverted predator would actually betroth himself to a child.
lines.zh: 是吗。那我猜，把 Tsukasa 抵押给随便哪个愿意跟一个孩子订婚的变态捕食者，就是{i}最好{/i}的选择了。

lines.en: : She’s not much younger than you, Touka. Do you really believe a few years makes that much of a difference?
lines.zh: 她也没比你小多少，Touka。你真觉得差几岁就有那么大区别吗？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween16
: Yes, actually. Which is why I also have no qualms with asking you to stay out of that aspect of my life and focus instead on those where your opinion is wanted.
lines.zh: 是的，真的。所以我才会毫不犹豫地要求你别插手我生活的这一面，把注意力放在别人需要你意见的地方。

lines.en: : You’ve gotten quite good at standing up to me, darling. I knew sending you off on your own would change you, but I’d be lying if I said I expected it to be {i}this{/i} drastic.
lines.zh: 你现在很敢顶撞我了，亲爱的。我早就知道放你一个人出去会改变你，可要说我想到会{i}这么{/i}彻底，那是在撒谎。

lines.en: : I’m not {i}changing{/i} at all. I’m just noticing things I never had before.
lines.zh: 我根本{i}没有变{/i}。我只是注意到了以前从未注意过的东西。

lines.en: : Oh, you’re changing. But love can do that to a person. Just like how love is what turned {i}me{/i} into the woman you suddenly have so many issues with.
lines.zh: 哦，你是在变。可爱情就是能让人变成这样。就像爱情把{i}我{/i}变成了你如今这么多意见的那个女人。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween17
: If this love you speak of is for your children, you certainly have an odd way of showing it.
lines.zh: 如果你说的这份爱是给你的孩子的，那你的表达方式可真够奇怪的。

lines.en: : It’ll make more sense when my time has come and gone and {i}you{/i} sit atop the throne this family has built.
lines.zh: 等我的时代过去、由{i}你{/i}坐上这个家族建起的王座时，你就明白了。

lines.en: : But, in the meantime, perhaps you should just trust me? I haven’t led you astray so far, have I?
lines.zh: 不过在那之前，也许你该信任我？我到目前为止也没把你带偏过，对吧？

lines.en: : Astray? No. Just into the arms and sights of a man who could ruin my life at any moment.
lines.zh: 带偏？没有。只是把我送进一个随时能毁掉我一生的男人的怀抱和视线里。

lines.en: : His {i}arms,{/i} you say?
lines.zh: 他的{i}怀抱{/i}，你是说？

lines.en: : It was a figure of speech, Mother. He’s yet to lay a finger on me.
lines.zh: 那只是个比喻，母亲。他连一根手指都没碰过我。

lines.en: : He has a surprising amount of willpower when he really applies himself, doesn’t he?
lines.zh: 他真要认真起来，自制力还挺惊人的，不是吗？

lines.en: : Yes. I just struggle to understand why he only {i}exercises{/i} such restraint with me when I am twice the woman any of those girls could ever hope to be.
lines.zh: 是啊。我只是想不通，既然我比那些女孩里任何一个都强上一倍，他为什么只对我{i}施展{/i}这种自制。

lines.en: : Given what he said to you in the past, I imagine he just has a very strange relationship with mothers.
lines.zh: 鉴于他以前对你说过那些话，我想他跟母亲这个角色之间的关系大概很古怪。

lines.en: : Don’t we all?
lines.zh: 谁不是呢？

lines.en: : The fortunate ones, maybe. Or {i}unfortunate{/i} depending on the circumstances. For I know you’ve abhorred me lately, but you still {i}respect{/i} me. Isn’t that right?
lines.zh: 也许幸运的人是这样。或者{i}不幸{/i}，取决于境遇。因为我知道你最近很厌恶我，可你仍然{i}尊重{/i}我。对吧？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween18
: I don’t {i}abhor{/i} you, Mother. I just don’t understand you as well as I thought I did. And that is...extremely irritating to me as it ultimately results in me questioning my actions and choices.
lines.zh: 我并不{i}厌恶{/i}你，母亲。我只是不像我以为的那样了解你。而这……让我极其烦躁，因为它最终会让我开始质疑自己的行为和选择。

lines.en: : I know there’s a method to this madness. You wouldn’t be here today if that were not the case.
lines.zh: 我知道这疯狂背后是有章法的。如果不是这样，你今天就不会站在这里。

lines.en: : But without an understanding of what that {i}madness{/i} is, I struggle to perceive it as anything else at all.
lines.zh: 可如果弄不清那份{i}疯狂{/i}到底是什么，我就很难把它看成别的东西。

lines.en: : Especially when I’m learning every day that there may be more to {i}all{/i} of this place than I initially believed.
lines.zh: 尤其是我每天都在发现，这个地方{i}一切{/i}的背后，也许比我最初以为的还要复杂。

lines.en: : Oh? Is this gossip I hear? Spill the tea, Touka. Have you heard that phrase before? Tea? How fun. You young people have the most curious vernacular.
lines.zh: 哦？我这是听到八卦了吗？说来听听，Touka。你听过这个说法吗？八卦？真有意思。你们年轻人的行话可真稀奇。

lines.en: : Mother, I have a question that is going to sound insane.
lines.zh: 母亲，我有个问题，听起来会很离谱。

lines.en: : And I ask that you simply answer yes or no, but I imagine you will not honor that request as most questions can not be fully answered in such a way.
lines.zh: 我希望你只用是或否来回答，不过我想你多半不会照做，因为大多数问题都没法这样答全。

lines.en: : Oh? Well, let’s hear it then. It seems rather serious based on your tone.
lines.zh: 哦？那说来听听吧。听你的语气，这事似乎挺严重。

lines.en: : Is the body of my classmate’s mother buried beneath the everblooming sakura?
lines.zh: 我同学的母亲的尸体，是不是埋在那棵四季盛开的樱花树下？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween19
: Why, that {i}does{/i} sound insane. Pray tell, where did you get that idea?
lines.zh: 哎呀，这{i}确实{/i}听起来很离谱。敢问你是从哪儿得来这个念头的？

lines.en: : A reliable source. One who knows far more about...basically {i}everything{/i} than anyone I’ve ever encountered.
lines.zh: 一个可靠的来源。一个比我见过的任何人都要懂……基本上{i}一切{/i}的人。

lines.en: : Even this family?
lines.zh: 连这个家族也算？

lines.en: : No...They’d have no way of knowing anything that goes on here as even {i}I{/i} do not yet understand everything that occurs within these walls.
lines.zh: 不……他们不可能知道这里发生的事，因为就连{i}我{/i}都还没弄懂这堵墙里发生的一切。

lines.en: : But there’s a poem she showed me that...very well {i}could{/i} be naught more than flowery symbolism both literally and figuratively that...
lines.zh: 但她给我看了一首诗，那首诗……{i}很可能{/i}只不过是些花里胡哨的象征，无论字面还是比喻意义上，它……

lines.en: : Well, it sounded like it was talking about our tree. And combined with your interest in both Sensei {i}and{/i} the seemingly omniscient knowledge of this classmate-
lines.zh: 嗯，听起来像是在说我们那棵树。再结合你对 Sensei 的兴趣，{i}以及{/i}这个同学那种仿佛无所不知的知识——

lines.en: : You believe her.
lines.zh: 你信她。

lines.en: : {size=-2}I...can not {i}refute{/i} her. Not nearly as much as I want to at least. For this claim sounds so extremely bizarre, but...so specific that it provides the {i}illusion{/i} of merit even if none actually exists.{/size}
lines.zh: {size=-2}我……{i}无法反驳{/i}她。至少远不如我希望的那样能反驳。因为这个说法听起来极其离奇，可又……具体得让人{i}误以为{/i}它有道理，即使实际上一点道理都没有。{/size}

lines.en: : And the classmate that raised this concern to you is Nodoka Nagasawa, I presume?
lines.zh: 那么，向你提出这个疑问的同学，我想是 Nodoka Nagasawa 吧？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween20
: Yes, but...how did you-
lines.zh: 是的，可是……你怎么——

lines.en: : I’d be foolish {i}not{/i} to know the name of the girl who's been consistenly upstaging you in every single academic field through two different schools now.
lines.zh: 我要是{i}不{/i}知道那个女孩的名字才叫蠢——她在两所学校里、每一门学科上都一直压你一头。

lines.en: : Excellent writer as well. Have you picked up “The Light of Last Summer” yet? Excellent read. Quite relevant to your...{i}situation{/i} too.
lines.zh: 她文笔也很出色。你看了《去年夏日之光》吗？非常好的书。而且跟你现在的……{i}处境{/i}也挺贴切。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween21
: Curious businesswoman, though. It takes a very {i}odd{/i} mind to conceptualize and subsequently invent a four-sided sex toy.
lines.zh: 不过她还是个挺奇怪的商人。要想出并真的发明出一个四面的性玩具，脑子得{i}相当古怪{/i}才行。

lines.en: : I...know little of such a device. But yes. That is the girl I’m referring to. But the classmate whose mother is thought to be buried beneath our tree is-
lines.zh: 我……对那种器具了解不多。不过是的，我说的就是那个女孩。但那个被认为母亲埋在我们树下的同学是——

lines.en: : None other than your teacher’s very own niece-turned-daughter, Ami Arakawa.
lines.zh: 不是别人，正是你那位老师的亲外甥女、如今成了他女儿的 Ami Arakawa。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween22
: Correct?
lines.zh: 对吧？

lines.en: : It’s {i}true{/i} then?
lines.zh: 那是{i}真的{/i}了？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween23
: Now, I never said {i}that.{/i} There are just very few girls in your class with dead mothers linked directly to poetry.
lines.zh: 我可没说过{i}这话{/i}。只是你们班上有死去的母亲、还和诗直接扯上关系的女生，实在没几个。

lines.en: : This is why I wanted a yes or a no. Complicating the answer is just going to make me even more confused.
lines.zh: 所以我才想要一个是或否。你把答案搞复杂，只会让我更糊涂。

lines.en: : Well, let me ask {i}you{/i} a question then. For what reason would we bury the body of some woman beneath a tree?
lines.zh: 那么，换{i}我{/i}来问你一个问题。我们有什么理由要把某个女人的尸体埋在树下？

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween24
: I can’t even completely discern your motivations for having Sensei become Tsukasa’s sex-tutor yet and you expect me to figure out the answer to {i}that?!{/i}
lines.zh: 我连你让 Sensei 去当 Tsukasa 的性教育老师的动机都还没完全看明白，你居然指望我想出{i}那个{/i}的答案？！

lines.en: : I don’t know! You do weird things sometimes! This could very well be one of those!
lines.zh: 我不知道！你有时候就是会做奇怪的事！这很可能就是其中之一！

lines.en: : There’s no need to yell, dear. I don’t want {i}you{/i} getting exhausted either.
lines.zh: 没必要喊，亲爱的。我也不想让{i}你{/i}累着。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween25
: There’s no one buried beneath the tree. And there’s no need for you to concern yourself with it when there are much bigger things out there you must be worrying about instead.
lines.zh: 树下没有埋任何人。你也不必为这个操心，外面还有大得多的事等着你去担心。

lines.en: : Like...what?
lines.zh: 比如……什么？

lines.en: : Yourself. Your friendships. Your {i}relationships.{/i} Things that will advance both your life and your career.
lines.zh: 你自己。你的友情。你的{i}感情{/i}。那些能推进你人生和事业的东西。

lines.en: : If we honored or delved into every single rumor about our family, we’d never get anything done. So the best course of action, more often than not, is to simply ignore them.
lines.zh: 要是我们对家族的每一条传言都当真、都去深挖，那什么都干不成了。所以大多数时候，最好的做法就是干脆无视它们。

lines.en: : And if you’re lying to me?...
lines.zh: 那如果你是在骗我呢？……

lines.en: : Then I’m lying for a reason.
lines.zh: 那我撒谎也是有理由的。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween26
: But I suppose {i}that{/i} could be a lie as well, couldn’t it?
lines.zh: 不过我想{i}那句话{/i}本身也可能是谎言，不是吗？

lines.en: : Quite the paradox, don’t you think?
lines.zh: 挺悖论的，你不觉得吗？

lines.en: : I don’t...really know what {i}to{/i} think anymore...
lines.zh: 我……真的不知道该{i}怎么{/i}想了……

lines.en: scene black
: Then take that as your sign to stop thinking about it at all. We’re far too important to worry about things like {i}gardening.{/i} We have workers for that.
lines.zh: 那就把这当成信号，干脆别再想了。我们太重要了，不该为{i}园艺{/i}这种事操心。那种事有工人做。

lines.en: : I...suppose that is true. And that someone would have likely...already uncovered such a thing if it were actually there...
lines.zh: 我……想是这样。而且如果真有那种东西，大概早就……被人发现了……

lines.en: : Exactly. Now, why don’t we get back to enjoying ourselves? You skipped out on your Christmas party to be with {i}me{/i} this year, didn’t you?
lines.zh: 没错。好了，我们继续好好享受吧？你今年为了陪{i}我{/i}，连圣诞派对都没去，对吧？

lines.en: : Yes, but-
lines.zh: 是的，不过——

lines.en: : Wait, Christmas? What’s-
lines.zh: 等等，圣诞？什么——

lines.en: : Ah! Silly me. Christmalloween, I mean. That’s enough wine for {i}me{/i} tonight.
lines.zh: 啊！我真糊涂。是圣诞万圣节，我是说。{i}我{/i}今晚的酒就到这儿吧。

lines.en: : Uhh...okay. But-
lines.zh: 呃……好吧。可是——

lines.en: : Actually, on second thought, why don’t you buzz in one of the butlers? I’d like you to get a taste of the Château Mouton Rothschild that came in this morning. And one more glass won’t kill me.
lines.zh: 不过再想想，你叫个管家进来吧？我想让你尝尝今早送来的 Château Mouton Rothschild。再来一杯也喝不死我。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween27
: So you like {i}really{/i} saw them doing it? Up close?
lines.zh: 所以你{i}真的{/i}看见他们做了？近距离？

lines.en: : Why are we talking about this again?! Chinami thought we escaped that topic!
lines.zh: 我们怎么又聊这个了？！Chinami 还以为我们逃过这个话题了！

lines.en: : I can’t help it, okay?! First, he did it in front of me. {i}Then{/i} he did it in front of you! Pattern recognition, Chinami! He could be doing this on purpose {i}to{/i} show us!
lines.zh: 我忍不住嘛，好吗？！先是在我面前做。{i}然后{/i}又在你面前做！这是模式识别啊，Chinami！他可能是故意做给我们{i}看{/i}的！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween28
: Chinami doesn’t think so...She was asleep when it happened and...big sis Chika wasn’t even home yet when Papa fell asleep too, so...
lines.zh: Chinami 不这么想……事发时她睡着了，而且……爸爸睡着的时候，Chika 姐姐还没回家呢，所以……

lines.en: : She...She thinks this time was just a coincidence...
lines.zh: 她……她觉得这次只是巧合……

lines.en: : {i}Or{/i} Jeeves is actually a lolicon!
lines.zh: {i}或者{/i} Jeeves 其实是个萝莉控！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween29
: Chinami acknowledges the possibility of this and is suddenly more reluctant to invite Papa into the bath with her. Things are too real now.
lines.zh: Chinami 承认有这个可能，而且突然不太想叫爸爸一起洗澡了。现在一切都太真实了。

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween30
: Taking a bath with him is such a good way to find out, though!
lines.zh: 不过跟他一起洗澡是查明真相的好办法啊！

lines.en: : Find out what?! How to cross a line we’d need to move to Alabama just to live with?!
lines.zh: 查明什么？！查明怎么跨过一条我们得搬到 Alabama 才能坦然面对的界线？！

lines.en: : Where is Alabama?!
lines.zh: Alabama 在哪儿？！

lines.en: : I don’t know! I’ve just heard that this would be normal there!
lines.zh: 我不知道！我只是听说在那儿这很正常！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween31
: Chinami, you have a real chance to make a scientific breakthrough here.
lines.zh: Chinami，你现在有个真正能取得科学突破的机会。

lines.en: : Chinami doesn’t {i}want{/i} to make a scientific breakthrough here! She doesn’t look at her papa that way! How many times does she have to tell you that?!
lines.zh: Chinami {i}不想要{/i}什么科学突破！她才不会用那种眼光看她爸爸！她要说多少遍你才明白？！

lines.en: : You don’t need to {i}do{/i} anything! You just need to find out if his penis gets hard or not. Because if it {i}does,{/i} it means-
lines.zh: 你什么都不用{i}做{/i}！你只需要弄清楚他的鸡巴会不会硬。因为如果{i}会{/i}，那就说明——

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween32
: Chinami knows what it means! And if Tsukasa is so desperate to make a scientific breakthrough, maybe {i}she{/i} should be the one to do it!
lines.zh: Chinami 知道那说明什么！要是 Tsukasa 这么想搞科学突破，也许{i}她{/i}该自己去做！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween33
: Fine! Then maybe I {i}will!{/i}
lines.zh: 好！那我也许{i}就去做{/i}！

lines.en: : Good!
lines.zh: 很好！

lines.en: : Yeah! It {i}is{/i} good! Coward!
lines.zh: 对！{i}确实{/i}很好！胆小鬼！

lines.en: : Pervert!
lines.zh: 变态！

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween34
: Mngh...
lines.zh: 嗯唔……

lines.en: : Hmmf...
lines.zh: 哼嗯……

lines.en: scene tsukiokamalloween35
: So, like...did you see how big it was?
lines.zh: 那么……你看见它有多大了？

lines.en: : {i}Huge.{/i} Big sis Chika must be the strongest girl in the world.
lines.zh: {i}特别大。{/i} Chika 姐姐一定是全世界最厉害的女生。

lines.en: scene black
: How huge? Show me with your hands.
lines.zh: 有多大？用手比给我看。

lines.en: : Like, um...uhh...this?
lines.zh: 就是，嗯……呃……这么大？

lines.en: : What? No way. You’re lying. That’s physically impossible. The human body can’t fit more than like four inches inside, max. That’s an undisputed fact.
lines.zh: 什么？不可能。你在撒谎。生理上根本不可能。人体里面最多也就塞得下四英寸，顶天了。这是不争的事实。

lines.en: : Or maybe it was...more like this?
lines.zh: 还是说……更像是这样？

lines.en: : That’s even bigger!
lines.zh: 这更大了！
